title: Melbourne Cup racehorse So You Are found dead in a skip
content:
The body of a leading dead race horse has been found dumped in a skip at a waste facility in Australia.

Melbourne Cup starter So You Are was euthanised after medics were unable to cure a bout of severe colic on Monday, a fortnight after the five-year-old had finished eighth in the race — widely considered one of the most prestigious in the sport.

Vets used anaesthesia before putting down the horse — owned by Stuart Ramsey and his wife Trish — but instead of being buried, it was found in a large metal skip by tradesman Gregg Jowett in Sydney later that day.

In a video uploaded to social media on Monday, Mr Jowett showed the horse in the skip and said to camera: “That can’t be normal… does anyone know if that’s legal? Disgusted by that. Please let me know if I’m wrong but that’s not normal.”

The horse was later identified as So You Are by its markings.

In a statement uploaded to his X account on Tuesday, So You Are’s trainer Trainer Bjorn Baker said: “Like everyone ​who has seen the footage, I am deeply distressed by the ⁠handling of So You Are’s remains.

“He was a much-loved horse, and he deserved to be treated with dignity ​and respect after his death.

“I understand the specialist hospital facility REC Equine Specialists are investigating the circumstances and I expect a full explanation of what occurred.

“My thoughts remain with the Ramsey family and with all my staff, for whom this has compounded an already devastating loss.”

In a statement to news.com.au, Racing New South Wales, the industry regulator for the state, said that the horse was being held at the waste facility temporarily while awaiting burial, but that the situation was “distressing” and “totally unacceptable”.

Racing New South Wales added that guidelines state “a licensed landfill is the preferred option for animals who have died via euthanasia due to the chemicals involved in the process” but that the horse should nevertheless have been buried sooner.

REC Equine Specialist said in a statement released to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation that it was sorry.

It said: “So You Are was in our care. We did not carry out the burial ourselves, but we chose the provider and the arrangements, and we take full responsibility for that.”

It added that work is ongoing to establish “processes to ensure it never happens again”.

Waste management company Cleanaway — which runs the Lucas Heights landfill in Sydney where the horse was found — told the ABC that So You Are had arrived in a small tipper truck which was not allowed on the landfill site “for safety reasons”.

It added: “In accordance with established procedures, the carcass was transferred into a skip bin to enable ​its safe disposal at the landfill.”

The Athletic has contacted REC Equine Specialist and Racing New South Wales for comment.

So You Are had gained its place in the Melbourne Cup after three consecutive wins which included the Group 3 Colin Stephen Quality, the ATC St Leger and the Group 3 Bendigo Cup. It had won eight of his 29 races in total.
